note: Hand-set priors, not estimates. Tilts run from -2 (headwind) to +2 (tailwind) relative to markets today. The president keeps the veto under every outcome, so Congress mostly matters through what it blocks, budget and debt-limit fights, and oversight. Edit freely.

tilts.name: Banks & financials
tilts.why: Deregulation momentum continues under unified control; a Democratic Congress adds oversight and hearings.

tilts.name: Oil & gas
tilts.why: Permitting and leasing changes need Congress to stick; a Democratic Congress stalls them.

tilts.name: Defense
tilts.why: Defense budgets pass more easily with one party; divided control means continuing resolutions and shutdown risk.

tilts.name: Clean energy
tilts.why: Either Democratic chamber blocks further rollback of energy tax credits.

tilts.name: Pharma & managed care
tilts.why: Drug pricing and insurer oversight get more floor time under a Democratic Congress.

tilts.name: Small caps
tilts.why: Small caps are the most sensitive to domestic tax and regulatory changes.

tilts.name: Long Treasuries
tilts.why: Gridlock makes new deficit-financed tax or spending bills less likely, which eases supply pressure on long bonds.
